mentions.text: It is very common across the industry to learn user embeddings to power personalized recommendations (Covington et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2020; Grbovic and Cheng, 2018; Zhang et al., 2020; Li et al., 2019; Pi et al., 2019).

One alternative that has shown promise is to directly build ranking models to generate personalized recommendations using sequential information from a user’s recent engagement (Chen et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2019; Pi et al., 2019; Pi et al., 2020).
There is limited work on leveraging the complete user action sequences (Fazelnia et al., 2022).
We introduce PinnerFormer, an end-to-end learned user embeddings via sequence modeling to encode long-term user interest (Pancha et al., 2022).

Each Pin at Pinterest is represented with a PinSage (Ying et al., 2018) embedding, which is an aggregation of visual (Jing et al., 2015; Gusev and Xu, 2020), text annotations (Mikolov et al., 2013; Mao et al., 2016), and engagement information (Eksombatchai et al., 2018) for a Pin.
In PinnerFormer, we model the sequence of user actions using a transformer model architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017).

We choose to use PreNorm residual connections, applying Layer Normalization before each block, as this approach has been shown to improve stability of training (Nguyen and Salazar, 2019; Wang et al., 2019).

In our offline evaluations, we observed superior performance compared to the previous baseline (Pancha et al., 2022) and tuned the parameters to strike a good balance between infrastructure cost and performance gains, i.e. MM=255, PP=100.
In the control group, the previous production model used a weighted average of a user’s top kk PinnerSage embeddings as a feature (Pal et al., 2020).
